title: Normalize spack version strings to conda-valid versions
description: Spack versions like '1.2.0-2024-08-16' contain hyphens, which conda/rattler forbids in version strings (regex ^[*.+!_0-9a-z]+$). This makes packages like rapidjson unsolvable by pixi ('no candidates found'). Transform disallowed chars (notably '-') to '_' consistently for both package versions and dependency pins in meta_from_spec.
close_reason: Added conda_version() normalizer in conda.py mapping illegal chars (esp. hyphens) to underscore; applied in meta_from_spec for package version and dependency pins. Tests added.

title: conda: unify closure Spack prefixes onto one placeholder to relocate rodata/text dependency paths
description: After the $ORIGIN rpath pass, binaries/text still embed absolute Spack paths into other closure packages (e.g. tar's compiled-in pigz/xz/rmt paths). Conda allows one prefix_placeholder per file, so only the own prefix is remapped today. Rewrite every closure-prefix occurrence in a file to a single common placeholder (the shortest referenced prefix) at conversion time; conda's install-time replacement then maps them all to the env prefix, because every <pkgprefix>/<sub> lands at <env>/<sub> in the merged layout. Binary rewrite is length-preserving (null-pad within the enclosing NUL-delimited segment); text is free. Record the common placeholder; extend the length limit accordingly.
close_reason: Implemented relocate.unify_prefix_refs: folds every closure-prefix reference onto one common placeholder (shortest referenced); binary length-preserving via NUL-segment shrink, text free. Wired into scan_prefix after the $ORIGIN pass with a common-root gate; records folded placeholder + feeds length limit. Verified on real tar binary (rmt + pigz/bzip2/xz/zstd all map to <env>/..., ELF valid). 76 tests pass.

title: conda: rewrite ELF RPATHs to $ORIGIN-relative for store-independent relocation
description: Spack binaries carry absolute RPATHs into per-package store prefixes (own + dependency prefixes). Conda merges all packages into one env prefix, so converted packages must have RPATHs rewritten to $ORIGIN-relative form to link without the Spack store. Implement a pure-Python ELF RPATH/RUNPATH rewriter (in-place shrink, no patchelf) that maps any converted-closure prefix to $ORIGIN. Apply during build; recompute sha256/size; add --origin-rpaths/--no-origin-rpaths (default on).
close_reason: Implemented pure-Python ELF RPATH/RUNPATH -> $ORIGIN rewriter (spaxi.relocate); wired through scan_prefix/build_conda_package/convert_spec with full-closure prefix set; --origin-rpaths default on. Verified on real spack binaries via readelf: libzstd.so RPATH -> $ORIGIN, bin/zstd -> $ORIGIN/../lib with no absolute store paths, exec bit preserved. 69 tests pass.

title: conda: build empty metapackage for payload-less bundle packages (e.g. glx)
description: spaxi conda aborts with 'no payload files found' on Spack bundle/glue packages like glx@1.4 whose install prefix holds only .spack. Such packages are legitimate runtime-dependency nodes, so they must exist in the channel to keep dependents resolvable. Build them as empty conda metapackages instead of raising.
close_reason: conda.build_conda_package no longer raises on empty payload; builds a valid empty metapackage (empty paths.json/files, empty pkg tar) so bundle packages like glx convert and remain resolvable by dependents. Updated tests.

title: conda: re-add intra-package file-scan pool (scan is IO/hash-bound, complements zstd)
description: Real logs show scan time tracks file COUNT not bytes (boost 16k files/184MiB=19s; mkl 4.9GiB=12s), i.e. filesystem-metadata + sha256 bound, both GIL-released and IO-latency bound. Serial per-package scan is the build long pole (llvm 27s scan). Re-add a shared, capped file-scan executor (removed earlier under the wrong assumption scan was CPU-bound); it complements CPU-bound zstd since scan and compress are different phases. Keep the zstd budget.
close_reason: Re-added shared file-scan pool (cap 16) beside the zstd budget. Scan is IO/hash-bound (GIL-released), complements CPU-bound zstd. Benchmarked solo big package 1.50->0.19s (16t, 8x); sha256 saturates ~16 so cap there. 82 tests pass.

title: conda: batch discovery via 'spack find -d' (constant spack calls, not O(2N))
description: Discover phase is 36s (~38% of runtime), dominated by spack subprocess startup: ~2 calls per unique node. 'spack find -d --json /root' returns the whole DAG as full node dicts in one call, and 'spack find -d --format {hash} {prefix} /root' returns all prefixes in one call (0.54s total regardless of size). Rewrite _discover to build node+prefix maps from these two batch calls (plus per-node resolve/prefix fallback), traversing in-memory.
close_reason: Added Spack.dag_nodes/dag_prefixes (spack find -d, one call each); _discover builds node+prefix maps from them with per-node fallback. Constant 3 spack calls regardless of tree size. 82 tests pass incl. batch + fallback unit tests.

title: conda: multithreaded zstd via shared budget; drop inner file-scan pool
description: Build tail dominated by single-threaded zstd level-19 on a few huge packages (-j4 == -j32). Add conda.ZstdThreadBudget(J): each package requests zstd threads proportional to payload; a lone big package in the tail gets most of the budget, small ones get 1, with a floor of 1 for bounded overcommit. Revert per-file scan pool to serial (GIL/IO-bound, only ~2x) so the CPU budget goes to GIL-free zstd. Benchmarked 400MB incompressible level-19: 58.8s->16.1s (4t)->11.7s (16t).
close_reason: Added conda.ZstdThreadBudget(J); payload-proportional zstd thread requests with floor 1; reverted scan to per-package serial. Benchmarked 400MB level-19: 58.8->16.1(4)->11.7s(16). 81 tests pass.

title: conda: parallelize per-file relocation scan; phase timing logs; faster prefix detection
description: Build phase tail dominated by single big packages scanned serially (200% CPU at -j32). Parallelize scan_prefix's per-file loop via a separate (deadlock-free) file pool, capped since the work is GIL/IO/memory-bound and saturates ~4-8 threads. Replace O(prefixes x filesize) referenced-prefix detection with a single anchored pass. Add phase-completion timing (discover/build) and per-package scan/archive/compress elapsed logs.
close_reason: Parallelized scan_prefix per-file loop via separate capped file pool; single-pass anchored prefix detection; phase timing logs. Benchmarked ~2x on large-file scan (saturates ~4-8, hence cap). 80 tests pass incl. executor==serial equivalence.

title: conda: memoize spack find during discovery (shared deps resolved once)
description: convert._discover called spack.resolve_one once per dependency EDGE, so heavily-shared nodes (glibc, gcc-runtime) triggered a spack find per dependent. Memoize resolve_one and prefix by hash so each unique node hits spack once.
close_reason: Memoized resolve_one and prefix by hash in _discover (shared deps resolved once); added deterministic (len,str) tie-break for the unified placeholder for reproducible builds. Unit test proves shared-dep resolved once; determinism verified across PYTHONHASHSEED. 77 tests pass.

title: conda: replace noisy per-package prefix note with a single channel-wide relocation-limit summary
description: Every built package prints 'end-user env prefix must be < N chars', even packages with no binary prefix embedding (meaningless) and off-by-one (<= is correct). The real constraint is channel-wide: the minimum placeholder length across packages that contain binary-relocated files. Compute prefix_limit only when binary placeholders exist and print one summary line.
close_reason: build_conda_package returns BuildResult(path, prefix_limit); limit set only when binary files embed the prefix. Converted carries prefix_limit; CLI drops per-line note and prints one channel-wide summary ('at most N characters, tightest: X'). Fixed off-by-one (<= not <). 60 tests pass.

title: conda: parallelize package builds (-j/--jobs) and expose -z/--compression-level
description: Large trees are slow because each package's scan+hash+zstd runs serially. Split convert_spec into sequential discovery (spack find calls, DB-locked) then a ThreadPoolExecutor build pool (zstd/hashlib release the GIL). Serialize only the repodata.json update via a lock (split channel.add_package into stage_package + index_record). Add -j/--jobs N (0=CPUs) and -z/--compression-level (default 19, max 22).
close_reason: Two-phase convert_spec: sequential _discover (spack calls) then ThreadPoolExecutor build pool; repodata serialized via channel.stage_package/index_record + Lock. Added -j/--jobs (0=CPUs) and -z/--compression-level (1-22, default 19). 59 tests pass incl. parallel==serial equivalence.

Add a build-time FlagCollisionError guard for the (future) case where a real variant collides with a synthesized _set/hash key.

title: Variant selection UX: conda build string is opaque Spack hash
description: Multiple variants of one name@version convert to distinct .conda packages keyed by build string = Spack DAG hash (verified: zstd +programs vs ~programs coexist). Users select a variant only by pinning the hash: zstd = { version='1.5.7', build='<hash>' } (exact or glob both work; verified). Gaps: (1) repodata exposes no variant info (depends are identical), so an unpinned spec resolves to an arbitrary/impl-defined build (rattler picked +programs here, not guaranteed); (2) the build string is an opaque hash, not e.g. '+programs', so users must first map variant->hash out-of-band (spaxi output, spack find, or info/spack-spec.json). Consider encoding a short variant label into the build string and/or 'spaxi conda' printing a ready-to-paste build pin.
notes: PREFERRED MECHANISM (supersedes build-string encoding): repodata 'flags' field, CEP-45 'Simplified variant selection' (Accepted 2026-05-14; siblings CEP-43 conditional deps, CEP-44 extras). A package asserts flags: ["programs", "blas:mkl"] in info/index.json AND its repodata record; each flag matches ^[a-z0-9_]+(:[a-z0-9_]+)?$ (bare tag or ONE key:value). Selected in pixi.toml as: zstd = { version='1.5.7', flags=['programs'] } with glob support. VERIFIED WORKING in the user's pixi 0.73 against a hand-written repodata (repodata_version=2): flags=['programs'] installs, ['prog*'] installs, ['mpi'] -> no candidates. This is first-class & matchable, so BUILD STAYS = hash and the FILENAME stays name-version-hash.conda (no length/charset/uniqueness problems). Limits: charset [a-z0-9_]+one colon (sanitize Spack variant names/values; uppercase/./+ not allowed); inclusion semantics only; NO negative selection yet (CEP-45 defers ! exclude and ? match-if-present) -> encode 'off' states as positive flags (e.g. mpi:false) for negation, same as the defaults-encoding point. Producer side is fully in spaxi's control (channel.py writes repodata, conda.py writes index.json). Status caveat: prefix.dev calls the wire format 'repodata v3' (beta, not on conda-forge; rattler-build needs --v3); pixi/rattler consume & auto-detect. Recommend: emit flags from spack spec variants; keep build=hash.
close_reason: Resolved via CEP-45 flags mechanism (not build-string encoding): variants now first-class matchable; build stays = hash, filenames unchanged. See spaxi-9km.

title: spaxi conda: no discovery/sync of installed specs vs channel
description: To shadow a Spack install area, a provider must convert every newly-installed spec. Today 'spaxi conda' takes one SPEC and resolve_one() requires exactly one match. There is no command/flag to (a) enumerate all installed specs (spack find --json with no spec already returns them in Spack.find()), (b) diff their DAG hashes against build strings already in the channel repodata, and (c) convert only the missing ones. Also no pruning of channel packages whose spack install has been removed. Proposed: 'spaxi conda --all' or a 'spaxi sync' that closes this loop.

title: spaxi conda re-run: skip check happens after per-dep spack resolves
description: Re-running is idempotent (convert_spec skips when dest .conda exists, so no rebuild/zstd), but not cheap: for every visited node it calls spack.resolve_one('/<hash>') for each runtime dep BEFORE the dest.exists() skip check (convert.py:61-66 then :81). The .conda filename needs only name/version/hash from the node itself, so the skip could be decided before resolving deps. Also diamond deps (e.g. gcc-runtime) get re-resolved once per parent. Net: an all-present re-run still spawns ~O(nodes) 'spack find' subprocesses. Consider one 'spack find --json --deps' to load the whole DAG, and move the skip earlier.
